criteria.quote: "Why would a bird that cannot fly far need a half-mile cry?"
criteria.revision: Replace with: "What is Spearow saying when a cry carries over half a mile?" This creates a question the research can directly answer without implying an unsupported reason for its limited flight range.

criteria.quote: "Spearow stands only zero point three meters tall in total."
criteria.revision: Remove the 0.3-meter scene, since the supplied research does not state Spearow’s height. Replace it with a concrete supported contrast: its short wings make it inept at flying high or long distances, yet its loud, high-pitched cry carries over half a mile.

criteria.quote: "Why would a bird that cannot fly far need a half-mile cry?"
criteria.revision: Make the open loop about the cry’s meaning rather than its presumed purpose: "A Spearow cry travels over half a mile—but what does that echoing call mean?" Then withhold the danger-warning reveal until the fifth scene.

criteria.quote: "Spearow can't fly far. Its cry reaches a half-mile." / "That cry can be heard over half a mile away."
criteria.revision: Cut the repeated half-mile statement from one of these scenes. Build upward as: short wings limit high/long flight; Spearow still darts rapidly around its territory; its cry carries over half a mile; then reveal that echoing high cries mean Spearow are warning each other of danger.

criteria.quote: "The cry is not just loud. Its echoing high call is a shared warning that danger is nearby."
criteria.revision: Make this the sole late reveal: change the earlier sound scene to only establish the half-mile range, then reveal, "When that high, keening cry echoes all around, it means Spearow are warning each other of danger."

criteria.quote: "Spearow can't fly far. Its cry reaches a half-mile." / "Its short wings make flying high and far difficult." / "That cry can be heard over half a mile away."
criteria.revision: Merge or remove the overlapping flight/range scenes. Use the freed scene for the supported territorial detail: "Spearow flies around ceaselessly and makes high-pitched cries to protect its territory," creating a new step before the danger-warning meaning.

criteria.quote: "The cry is not just loud. Its echoing high call is a shared warning that danger is nearby."
criteria.revision: Align the ending with a revised opening promise. Open on what the distant cry means, then end with the explicit answer: "If Spearow’s high, keening cry is echoing all around, they’re warning each other that danger is nearby."

criteria.quote: "Which helps Spearow more: fast patrols or warning cries?"
criteria.revision: Make the split more grounded in the two documented behaviors without claiming the research can measure which is better: "For Spearow’s territory, what matters more: darting around at high speed, or a cry that warns other Spearow of danger from over half a mile away?"
